name: Adding fractions
note: To add fractions, both must describe parts of the same size. Rewrite each fraction with a common denominator, scaling the numerator by the same factor as the denominator, then add only the numerators. The denominator names the size of the part; it is not added. Example: 1/4 + 2/3 becomes 3/12 + 8/12 = 11/12. Sense check: the sum of two positive fractions must be larger than each of them.

name: Multiplying fractions
note: To multiply fractions, multiply numerator by numerator and denominator by denominator: a/b x c/d = (a x c)/(b x d). Multiplying by a number less than 1 takes a part of the original amount, so the result is smaller. Example: 1/3 x 3/4 = 3/12 = 1/4, which is smaller than 3/4. Multiplication makes a number bigger only when the multiplier is greater than 1.

name: Dividing fractions
note: To divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal. Keep the first fraction, flip the second (the divisor). Example: 2/5 divided by 1/3 = 2/5 x 3/1 = 6/5. Dividing by a number less than 1 asks how many small parts fit, so the answer is larger than the starting number. Division makes a number smaller only when the divisor is greater than 1.

name: Comparing decimals
note: Compare decimals place by place from the left, starting with the tenths. The number of digits after the point does not decide size. Example: 0.7 is greater than 0.65 because 7 tenths is more than 6 tenths. Writing both with the same number of decimal places helps: 0.70 versus 0.65.

name: Multiplying decimals
note: Multiply the numbers as if they were whole numbers, then count the total decimal places in both factors and place the point so the answer has that many decimal places. Example: 0.4 x 0.3: 4 x 3 = 12, two decimal places in total, so 0.12. Estimate first: 0.4 x 0.3 is less than both factors.

name: Operations with integers
note: Adding two negative numbers moves further left on the number line, so the result is negative: -4 + (-6) = -10. Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding its opposite: 9 - (-2) = 9 + 2 = 11. The rule that two negatives give a positive applies to multiplication and division, not to addition.

name: Order of operations
note: Evaluate brackets first, then powers, then multiplication and division from left to right, then addition and subtraction from left to right (BODMAS). Example: 10 - 6 / 3 = 10 - 2 = 8, not (10 - 6) / 3. Working strictly left to right gives a different, incorrect answer.

name: Like and unlike terms
note: Only like terms, terms with exactly the same variables raised to the same powers, can be added. 4p + 2p = 6p, but 4p + 2q cannot be combined and stays 4p + 2q. Adding a term to itself doubles it: y + y = 2y. Multiplying it by itself squares it: y x y = y squared.

name: Expanding brackets
note: The number outside a bracket multiplies every term inside it: 4(y + 5) = 4y + 20. A minus sign outside a bracket changes the sign of every term inside: -(y - 7) = -y + 7. With an expression like 8 - 3(y - 2), multiply first, -3 x y and -3 x -2, giving 8 - 3y + 6 = 14 - 3y.

name: Solving linear equations
ncert_topic: Class 8, Linear Equations in One Variable
note: An equation is a balance: whatever you do to one side, do to the other. To undo + 4, subtract 4 from both sides; to undo multiplying by 5, divide both sides by 5. Example: 5y + 4 = 29 gives 5y = 25, then y = 5. Check by substituting back: 5 x 5 + 4 = 29.

name: Exponents
note: An exponent counts repeated multiplication: 3 to the power 4 means 3 x 3 x 3 x 3 = 81, not 3 x 4. When multiplying powers of the same base, add the exponents: b^4 x b^2 = b^6. Any non-zero number raised to the power 0 equals 1, because dividing b^n by b^n gives 1 and leaves exponent n - n = 0.

name: Percentages
note: Percentage change is always measured against the original value: change divided by original, times 100. A rise from 40 to 50 is 10/40 = 25 percent. A percentage increase followed by the same percentage decrease does not return to the start, because the second percentage is taken of a different, larger amount: 200 up 20 percent is 240, down 20 percent is 192.

name: Sharing in a ratio
note: To share an amount in the ratio a:b, add the parts to get the total number of equal shares, a + b. Each share is the amount divided by a + b. Example: 60 in the ratio 1:4 gives 5 shares of 12, so 12 and 48. In a ratio 1:4 the first part is 1/5 of the total, not 1/4.

name: Algebraic identities
note: (a + b) squared means (a + b)(a + b). Multiplying out gives a squared + 2ab + b squared. The middle term 2ab is easy to forget. Example: (y + 5) squared = y squared + 10y + 25. Check with a number: if y = 1, (1 + 5) squared = 36 and 1 + 10 + 25 = 36.
